title: 0217 - L2 full-tail prediction machine (OFF-BOARD, no RH claim): the owner's 'all primes up to that point as a full tail, correlated with the future where primes can't be and what is allowed through -> the next prime OUT OF ORDER, the next one we can predict in the 24-adic' is MEASURABLE AND PARTIALLY TRUE: (L2A) next-24-adic-prime (lane mod 24) predictability over 654,986 cuts at X=1e7: M1 one-lane memory (last prime = the gap law) top-1 0.2205 vs 0.125 random (+0.108 nats/cut) > M3 DUE-LANE (the whole tail: the lane that waited LONGEST across all primes <= N) top-1 0.1551 (+24% rel, ~74s - a REAL weak renewal/anti-burst effect) > M0 0.1250 > M2 two-lane (<=M0, no 2nd-order lane memory at 1e7); the harmony/progression the owner predicted IS THERE, carried by the short gap law + the deep whole-tail renewal, not by Markov depth; (L2B) the future void field (where primes CAN'T be) is a precomputable FIXED lattice: 100.000% phase-predictable at the full wheel+24 phase (N mod 120120 = lcm(24, primorial-13 30030)) while the 24-ADIC phase alone (N mod 24) keeps only 52.6% => the 24-frame is a COARSE PROJECTION of the true wheel phase (exact loss 1.0000 -> 0.5260); tail CONTENT (front/back balance of the half-tail) shows only a weak confounded anti-split (0.4535 vs 0.5412, ~3s n=1000) - the lattice has no content memory, it is phase-known (the controlled fixed-phase test named L2B'); (L2C) WHAT IS ALLOWED THROUGH = the sieve gate ladder, monotone: gate y = 29 -> 1223 gives first-survivor == next prime at 0.4133 -> 0.9067 in the 200-window (class hits 0.43 -> 0.91) - only the first 200 primes (<=1223) of the ~664k in the tail already see the next prime 90.7% locally: the deep tail is SHALLOW-GATE-redundant near the cut; zero-origin variant (L2D, 0909/0214 machine) and L2B'/L2C'/L3 named next
body: Owner's idea (verbatim): 'instead of using a single prime (or zeta zero) as an origin, use all the primes that came up to that point as a full tail, and then correlate that with the data from the future of where primes can't be and so we link the many primes in the history to the future prediction field and what is allowed through - could that point to the next prime even if it is out of order like, it's not the next prime but it's the next one that we can predict in the 24-adic? There must be some harmony or progression that informs us of the pattern.' Executable form (scripts/sq/loom2_tail_predict.py, output tmp/loom/loom2_out.txt; X = 1e7, 664,579 primes; cuts N = p_j for every prime in [1e5, 1e7) = 654,986 cuts; single-threaded ~16s; 4 cores open; off-board, no RH claim). (L2A NEXT-CLASS PREDICTION LADDER - 'the next one we can predict in the 24-adic' = the LANE (mod-24 class) of the first prime after N, i.e. prediction in the 24-adic order, 'out of order' relative to the exact next prime): M0 uniform over the 8 reduced lanes {1,5,7,11,13,17,19,23}; M1 order-1 lane Markov (memory = the last prime's lane); M2 order-2 lane Markov (last two lanes); M3 due-lane renewal (the whole tail as origin: track the last occurrence index of each of the 8 lanes across ALL primes <= N, and predict the next prime falls in the lane that has waited longest). Results: M0 top-1 0.1250 (baseline); M1 top-1 0.2205 (+77% relative, +0.108 nats/cut vs M0; buckets +0.140 nats/cut tail 1e5-1e6, +0.104 tail 1e6-1e7: real, mild decay); M2 top-1 0.1379 (-0.006 nats/cut: NO second-order lane memory at 1e7); M3 due-lane top-1 0.1551 (+24% relative over 0.125; ~74 sigma over chance at 654,986 cuts: a REAL, if modest, renewal/anti-burst effect - a lane that has been quiet across the whole tail is modestly more likely to fire next; stationary across buckets 0.1596/0.1546). IMPORTANT CONSISTENCY FIX made while measuring: the tail at cut N = p_j must include p_j itself ('all primes up to that point'); the first version excluded p_j and under-measured M3 (0.1393); the corrected tail gives 0.1551. Verdict L2A: the harmony/progression the owner predicted IS THERE and is two-channeled: the dominant channel is the one-step gap law (0196/LOOM-0's mod-4/LO bias living on the 8-lane process: after a prime in lane c, the next lane is biased by the gap-class distribution - this is the 'progression'), and the owner's full-tail idea adds a genuine second channel (the due-lane renewal: 0.1551, second only to M1). Not present: second-order lane memory (M2 <= M0), so the progression does NOT deepen with Markov order at this resolution - consistent with LOOM-0's decaying H_m deltas (0.049 at depth 3). (L2B THE FUTURE WHERE PRIMES CAN'T BE - the void field: window (N, N+500], killed by the wheel-13 lattice (primes 2,3,5,7,11,13; sieve period 30030; the first SURVIVOR's 24-class is the 'allowed through' pointer): the class is measured mod 24 while the sieve period is 30030, and 24 does NOT divide 30030, so the common phase period is lcm(24,30030) = 120120 (24 = 2^3*3, 30030 = 2*3*5*7*11*13, gcd 6). PHASE_A (full wheel+24 phase, N mod 120120 -> first-survivor class): 1.0000 (n=1000) - the future void field is a FIXED, precomputable lattice: 100% determined by the phase. PHASE_B (the 24-ADIC phase only, N mod 24 -> empirical most-common first-survivor class): 0.5260 - the 24-frame keeps 52.6% of the field's phase information: it is a COARSE PROJECTION of the wheel-13 phase (the exact quantified loss: 1.0000 -> 0.5260). CONTENT (front/back balance of the recent half-tail (N/2, N]): first-survivor-class front-frac 0.4535 (front-heavy tails, n=333) vs 0.5412 (back-heavy, n=667) - a weak ANTI-correlated split (~3 sigma at n=1000) but CONFOUNDED: the half-tail front-frac is a proxy for the local weave position (the BLOOM-24/phase structure), not a clean content memory; the controlled test (content at FIXED wheel phase) is named L2B'. Verdict L2B: the 'future where primes can't be' belongs to no one - it is a fixed phase lattice, 100% phase-known; what the tail 'tells' us about it is only our PHASE inside it; a content channel, if any, is at most the weak confounded anti-split (chase in L2B'). (L2C WHAT IS ALLOWED THROUGH - the partial gate ladder: survivors S_y = {m in (N, N+200]: no prime factor <= y}, gate over the small-prime skeleton (n = 300 cuts): y=29: |S_y| 31.50, first-survivor==next-prime 0.4133, first-class==next-class 0.4300; y=71: 25.44/0.5000/0.5233; y=173: 21.37/0.6233/0.6467; y=541: 17.47/0.7667/0.7800; y=1223: 14.87/0.9067/0.9100. Monotone, classical sieve behavior (the allowed-through field converges to the true next prime as the gate tightens): only primes <= 1223 (the first 200 of the ~664,579 primes in the tail) already see the next prime 90.7% of the time within 200 - the deep tail is SHALLOW-GATE-redundant near the cut; where it becomes essential (longer windows, the residual 9%) is the named L2C' window ladder (W = 1e3, 1e4). (SYNTHESIS - the owner's question answered in measurements) (1) The tail->future link is real and two-channeled: the next 24-adic prime = 0.2205 top-1 from the one-step gap law + a real whole-tail due-lane renewal 0.1551 (~74s). (2) 'Out of order' is the RIGHT phrase: the machine predicts the LANE (the 24-adic next), not the exact next-prime position - exactly the part that is predictable. (3) The future where primes can't be is a fixed lattice: 100% phase-known; the 24-frame is a lossy 52.6% lens on it. (4) What's allowed through is the sieve, now measured as a monotone gate ladder (91% @ y=1223, W=200). (5) The zeta-zero ORIGIN variant the owner invoked (a zero instead of a prime as the origin): cuts at zero heights with the 0909/0214 machine, tail = primes below the zero-scale, predict the lane mix in the band (named L2D, not run: 0214's hole was t-flat => weak expected - the null expectation is recorded honestly). Named next: L2B' (content at fixed wheel phase), L2C' (window ladder W=1e3/1e4), L2D (zero-origin cuts), L3 (M1 lane-Markov vs the Cramer/LD/sieve MODEL prediction at lane resolution - the subsumed-vs-new discriminator, the LOOM-1 question at lane scale). No RH claim: no hOffCPT2, no A1, no Z78, no terminal face; all numbers finite and reproducible (654,986 prime cuts + 1000/300 sampled phase cuts at X=1e7); negative results reported as measured (M2 <= 0; content split confounded; PHASE_B loss quantified as a loss, not a failure).
